To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) news journalists have a higher risk for developing PTSD than the general population; (2) the risk of developing PTSD is higher when the news journalists have experienced a potentially traumatic event in the course of their work; (3) the risk of PTSD is higher when journalists have experienced a PTE in their personal life; and (4) the risk for developing depression and PTSD is higher when a journalist experiences a PTE in his/her personal life.
the exposure to potentially traumatic event is common within journalistic profession and depression mediates the relationship between potentially traumatic exposure and PTSD in news journalist.
exposure to potentially traumatic assignments during work assignments at the scene of a crisis and in personal life were predictors of post-traumatic symptomatology in news journalists.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between exposure to potentially traumatizing events and post-traumatic stress symptoms among news journalists.
the mediating effect between exposure to potentially traumatizing events and post-traumatic stress symptoms.
the mediating effect that depression has between the exposure to potentially traumatic experiences in the work and private life of news journalists and posttraumatic stress disorder.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the current study support the hypothesis that the relationship between PTE exposure and PTSD is mediated by depression.
the results of this study support the hypothesis that the exposure to potentially traumatic experiences at the scene and in personal lives is related to PTSD and depression in news journalists.

depression mediates the relationship between potentially traumatic events in personal life and at work, as well as the relationship between PTSD and exposure to potentially traumatic event in personal life and on the work place.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results indicate that the risk of developing PTSD is not only dependent on the number of traumatic events, but the level of depression is also an important predictor of the development of PTSD.
news journalists’ work is characterized by exposure to potentially traumatic experiences.
exposure to traumatic events is common in the journalistic work, but the development of posttraumatic stress disorder ( PTSD) and depression are less common.

the risk of developing PTSD is not only related to exposure to potentially traumatic experiences, but also to the level of depressive symptoms.
exposure to potentially traumatic assignments is common within journalistic assignments and it is important to understand the mechanisms behind the development of symptoms related to trauma history.
